# 2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game

The **2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game** was a National Football League (NFL) regular season game played on December 15, 2013, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. The Week 15 matchup featured two National Football Conference (NFC) teams fighting for playoff positioning. The Green Bay Packers defeated the Dallas Cowboys 37–36, overcoming a 23-point halftime deficit. The victory matched the largest comeback in Packers franchise history, equaling a record set in 1982 .

The game is notable for the statistical disparity between the two halves and the performance of Packers backup quarterback Matt Flynn, who started in place of the injured Aaron Rodgers. The Cowboys dominated the first half, leading 26–3 at intermission behind the play of quarterback Tony Romo and kicker Dan Bailey . However, Green Bay scored touchdowns on five consecutive possessions in the second half . The game was decided in the final minutes when Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo threw two interceptions, allowing Green Bay to take the lead on an Eddie Lacy touchdown run with 1:31 remaining .

The result had significant postseason implications. The victory kept Green Bay's playoff hopes alive, allowing them to eventually win the NFC North division, while the loss contributed to the Cowboys' elimination from playoff contention the following week . The game also generated significant media discussion regarding Dallas's play-calling strategy, specifically the decision to pass rather than run while holding a lead late in the fourth quarter, and the early departure of Cowboys receiver Dez Bryant from the field before the game clock had expired .

## Background

Heading into Week 15 of the 2013 NFL season, both teams held middling records but remained in contention for their respective division titles. The Dallas Cowboys entered the game with a 7–6 record, vying for the NFC East title . The Green Bay Packers held a 6–6–1 record and were competing for the NFC North .

The Packers were playing without their starting quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, who had suffered a broken collarbone in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears. Following the injury, the Packers struggled, losing or tying five consecutive games under backup quarterbacks Seneca Wallace, Scott Tolzien, and Matt Flynn . Flynn, who had been released by the Oakland Raiders and Buffalo Bills earlier in the 2013 season before returning to Green Bay, was named the starter for the game against Dallas .

The Cowboys possessed the league's worst-ranked defense entering the game but were favored to win by four points . Both teams were coming off losses in Week 14 .

## Game summary

### First half
The first half was controlled by the Dallas Cowboys, who capitalized on offensive efficiency and defensive stops. Dallas opened the scoring with a 47-yard field goal by Dan Bailey. Green Bay responded with a 57-yard field goal by Mason Crosby to tie the game at 3–3 .

Following the tie, the Cowboys scored 23 unanswered points. Bailey added field goals of 23, 43, and 50 yards . The Cowboys' offense, led by Tony Romo, found the end zone late in the first quarter when Romo connected with tight end Jason Witten for a 25-yard touchdown pass . In the second quarter, running back DeMarco Murray scored on a 1-yard touchdown run .

Green Bay's offense struggled to move the ball, with Matt Flynn completing 10 of 17 passes for only 114 yards and one interception in the first half . At halftime, the Cowboys held a commanding 26–3 lead, and statistical models and commentators viewed a Packers victory as highly improbable .

### Second half
The momentum shifted immediately in the third quarter. The Packers proceeded to score touchdowns on all five of their second-half possessions .

Green Bay opened the third quarter with an 80-yard drive, capped by a 13-yard touchdown pass from Flynn to Jordy Nelson . Dallas responded with a drive that stalled, resulting in a 50-yard field goal by Dan Bailey, extending their lead to 29–10 .

Flynn then led an 80-yard drive ending with a 3-yard touchdown pass to tight end Andrew Quarless, narrowing the deficit to 29–17 . Following a defensive stop, the Packers scored again early in the fourth quarter on an 11-yard touchdown pass to running back James Starks, bringing the score to 29–24 .

The Cowboys offense responded with a 10-play, 80-yard drive. Romo completed a 5-yard touchdown pass to Dez Bryant, who made a leaping catch in the back of the end zone. This extended the Dallas lead to 36–24 with approximately eight minutes remaining .

Green Bay answered quickly. Flynn directed another 80-yard drive, culminating in a 3-yard touchdown pass to James Jones. This cut the Dallas lead to 36–31 with 4:17 remaining in the game .

### Final minutes
With under three minutes remaining and holding a five-point lead, the Cowboys took possession. On a second-down play with 2:58 left, the Cowboys lined up to run the ball. However, quarterback Tony Romo checked out of the run play at the line of scrimmage after reading the defensive alignment. He attempted a pass to Miles Austin, but the throw was behind the receiver and was intercepted by Packers cornerback Sam Shields at midfield .

Following the interception, the Packers drove 50 yards in seven plays. Running back Eddie Lacy scored on a 1-yard touchdown run with 1:31 remaining. The Packers attempted a two-point conversion to extend the lead to three points, but the pass failed, leaving the score at 37–36 in favor of Green Bay .

The Cowboys had one final possession to drive into field goal range. On the second play of the drive, Romo attempted a pass to Cole Beasley. The pass was thrown behind the receiver and intercepted by Packers cornerback Tramon Williams. The play was initially ruled incomplete, but a replay review reversed the call, confirming the interception and sealing the victory for Green Bay .

## Statistical leaders

The game featured high offensive output from both teams. The Cowboys outgained the Packers in total yards 466 to 433 .

**Green Bay Packers**
* **Passing:** Matt Flynn – 26/39, 299 yards, 4 TD, 1 INT
* **Rushing:** Eddie Lacy – 21 carries, 141 yards, 1 TD
* **Receiving:** Jarrett Boykin – 6 receptions, 83 yards
* **Defense:** Tramon Williams (1 INT), Sam Shields (1 INT)

**Dallas Cowboys**
* **Passing:** Tony Romo – 29/48, 358 yards, 2 TD, 2 INT
* **Rushing:** DeMarco Murray – 18 carries, 134 yards, 1 TD
* **Receiving:** Dez Bryant – 11 receptions, 153 yards, 1 TD
* **Kicking:** Dan Bailey – 5/5 Field Goals (Long 50)

*Source: *

## Analysis and aftermath

### Historical significance
The 23-point comeback tied the Green Bay Packers' franchise record for the largest deficit overcome to win a game. The record was originally set in 1982 against the Los Angeles Rams . Packers head coach Mike McCarthy described the victory as "incredible" and noted the sheer emotion involved in the win . Players compared the atmosphere on the sideline during the comeback to their Super Bowl XLV victory .

### Criticism of Dallas play-calling
Following the game, the Cowboys' coaching staff and quarterback Tony Romo faced intense scrutiny regarding their clock management and play selection. Despite leading by five points with under three minutes remaining, and despite running back DeMarco Murray averaging 7.4 yards per carry, the Cowboys opted to pass the ball .

The interception by Sam Shields occurred on a play where Romo checked out of a called run play into a pass play. Head coach Jason Garrett confirmed post-game that the original call was a run, designed to force Green Bay to use their timeouts. Romo defended the decision to change the play, citing the Packers' defensive alignment which overloaded the box to stop the run. However, Romo admitted he did not protect the ball well enough on the subsequent throw .

Packers players expressed surprise and relief that Dallas abandoned the running game. Defensive tackle Ryan Pickett stated, "We're just happy they did. We were, like, 'OK, we'll take it,'" noting that the Cowboys' zone run scheme had been highly effective throughout the game .

### Dez Bryant early exit
Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant attracted media attention for leaving the field with 1:21 remaining on the clock, prior to the game's conclusion. Bryant walked to the locker room after the replay official confirmed the game-sealing interception by Tramon Williams. Bryant later apologized, stating his departure was due to being "too emotional" to watch the Packers kneel out the clock and that he had been crying . While former player Deion Sanders criticized the move as "absolutely... wrong," coach Jason Garrett defended Bryant's character while acknowledging he would address the importance of staying on the field .

### Season impact
The victory improved the Packers' record to 7–6–1, keeping them in contention for the NFC North. Aaron Rodgers returned from injury for the final game of the season, where the Packers defeated the Chicago Bears to win the division and secure a playoff berth .

The loss dropped the Cowboys to 7–7. Although they remained in contention for the NFC East until the final week of the season, they ultimately finished 8–8 and missed the playoffs for the fourth consecutive year .

Romo takes the blame for interceptions in 37-36 loss to Packers
===============================================================

"I think if you play long enough, you have plenty of big wins and tough losses," Dallas quarterback Tony Romo said after Sunday's game. "This is obviously a tough one."

![Image 11](https://www.wfaa.com/article/sports/nfl/cowboys/romo-takes-the-blame-for-interceptions-in-37-36-loss-to-packers/287-306006072) ![Image 12](http://content.wfaa.com/photo/2014/08/20/1215_tony_romo01_5740743_ver1.0.jpg)

Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo enters the locker room at AT&T Stadium in Arlington after the team's 37-36 loss to the Green Bay Packers on December 15, 2013.

Author: WFAA Staff

Published: 11:19 PM CST December 15, 2013

Updated: 11:19 PM CST December 15, 2013

[![Image 13: Facebook](https://www.wfaa.com/assets/shared-images/icons/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=1886819031630970&display=popup&href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wfaa.com%2Farticle%2Fsports%2Fnfl%2Fcowboys%2Fromo-takes-the-blame-for-interceptions-in-37-36-loss-to-packers%2F287-306006072&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wfaa.com%2Farticle%2Fsports%2Fnfl%2Fcowboys%2Fromo-takes-the-blame-for-interceptions-in-37-36-loss-to-packers%2F287-306006072)

ARLINGTON The Cowboys lost to the Green Bay Packers 37-36 on Sunday in a game where Dallas allowed the Packers to match their biggest comeback in franchise history.

The Cowboys could only watch as their 26-3 halftime lead evaporated in the final minutes of the game.

'It's a disappointing loss, there is no question about that,' Cowboys head coach Jason Garrett said.

'I think if you play long enough, you have plenty of big wins and tough losses,' Dallas quarterback Tony Romo added. 'This is obviously a tough one.'

The Cowboys had a five-point lead starting the final 4:17 of the game, but two interceptions thrown by Romo cost Dallas the game.

The first pick came with 2:58 left in the contest as Romo tried to get the ball to wide receiver Miles Austin.

'The idea was to run the ball and make them use the clock; run it and if we throw it, throw high percentage passes, keep the clock going, and make them use their time outs,' Garrett explained.

Instead, Romo chose to change the play.

'It's a run call that we have,' Romo said. 'We'll have it up three to five or six times a game. That specific time, obviously when I look back now, you should run the ball, because you throw an interception. You should never give them a chance to have the ball.'

'It's something we have accompanying some runs if he gets a bad look; that's what happened on the interception,' Garrett said. 'It was run call, though, that he threw the ball on.'

Dallas ran the ball only seven times in the second half, but the first interception led to the game-winning touchdown.

'They overloaded the side we were going to run the ball to, and I ended up throwing to the man that was one-on-one,' Romo said. 'The defense did a real good job of coming in. It's my fault for obviously putting the ball in position where the defense could make a play.'

The Packers drove 50 yards on seven plays after the interception to take a 37-36 lead. When the Cowboys got the ball back with a chance to take the lead back, there was 1:31 left in the game.

The Cowboys were able to run only two plays.

The first was a pass to Cole Beasley that gained nine yards.

The second was an another pass to Beasley, which Packers cornerback Tramon Williams intercepted to ice the game with 1:24.

'There was a miscommunication just how he was going to run that route,' Garrett said. 'I think he and Tony just weren't on the same page and how they played the defense. He ran up and ran out, and Tony was a little out in front of him with the ball.'

'Yeah, he ended up cutting his route off, and I threw it as if was continuing to go to sideline,' Romo said. 'We'll get that right. We'll go back and access the whole process and get it right.'

Romo's two interceptions were separated by only 1:34.

'The clock management by the Cowboys is worst that I've seen,' Fox analyst and former Cowboys quarterback Troy Aikman said during the national broadcast.

The Packers scored a touchdown on all five of their possessions in the second half, with drives of 80, 80, 22, 80 and 50 yards.

The loss hit an emotional Dez Bryant hard. The Cowboys; wide receiver left the field at AT&T Stadium with 1:04 still left on the clock.

Bryant tweeted after the game saying: 'I walked back to the locker room because I was emotional. It had nothing to do with my teammates. We had it. We fought and didn't finish.'

At 7-7, the loss leaves the Cowboys in the same position they were in when the day started. They still trail the 8-6 Eagles by one game. 6. Philadelphia lost as well, which means the Cowboys can still make the playoffs if they win their final two games of the season.

Dallas will be in Washington next week and close out the regular season against the Eagles at AT&T Stadium in Arlington on December 29.

Matt Flynn Overcomes Poor 1st Half, Leads Packers to Huge Comeback vs. Cowboys
==============================================================================

By[Patrick Schmidt](https://deathvalleyvoice.com/author/patrickschmidt)|

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=531030426978426&display=popup&href=https:%2F%2Fdeathvalleyvoice.com%2F2013%2F12%2F15%2Fmatt-flynn-overcomes-poor-1st-half-leads-packers-huge-comeback-vs-cowboys%2F)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Matt%20Flynn%20Overcomes%20Poor%201st%20Half%2C%20Leads%20Packers%20to%20Huge%20Comeback%20vs.%20Cowboys&url=https:%2F%2Fdeathvalleyvoice.com%2F2013%2F12%2F15%2Fmatt-flynn-overcomes-poor-1st-half-leads-packers-huge-comeback-vs-cowboys%2F)[](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https:%2F%2Fdeathvalleyvoice.com%2F2013%2F12%2F15%2Fmatt-flynn-overcomes-poor-1st-half-leads-packers-huge-comeback-vs-cowboys%2F&title=Matt%20Flynn%20Overcomes%20Poor%201st%20Half%2C%20Leads%20Packers%20to%20Huge%20Comeback%20vs.%20Cowboys)

![Image 3](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_fill,w_720,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/shape/cover/sport/681882672484fceb62500a2818f12860dccef8801fc1f1545bbbb90aef722870.jpg)

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=531030426978426&display=popup&href=https:%2F%2Fdeathvalleyvoice.com%2F2013%2F12%2F15%2Fmatt-flynn-overcomes-poor-1st-half-leads-packers-huge-comeback-vs-cowboys%2F)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Matt%20Flynn%20Overcomes%20Poor%201st%20Half%2C%20Leads%20Packers%20to%20Huge%20Comeback%20vs.%20Cowboys&url=https:%2F%2Fdeathvalleyvoice.com%2F2013%2F12%2F15%2Fmatt-flynn-overcomes-poor-1st-half-leads-packers-huge-comeback-vs-cowboys%2F)[](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https:%2F%2Fdeathvalleyvoice.com%2F2013%2F12%2F15%2Fmatt-flynn-overcomes-poor-1st-half-leads-packers-huge-comeback-vs-cowboys%2F&title=Matt%20Flynn%20Overcomes%20Poor%201st%20Half%2C%20Leads%20Packers%20to%20Huge%20Comeback%20vs.%20Cowboys)

Dec 15, 2013; Arlington, TX, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Matt Flynn (10) pitches the ball in the second quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tim Heitman-USA TODAY Sports

It was a [tale of two halves for Matt Flynn](https://deathvalleyvoice.com/2013/12/15/matt-flynn-struggling-mightily-green-bay-packers-vs-dallas-cowboys/) and the Green Bay Packers who trailed 26-3 at halftime after Flynn was a paltry 10-17 passing with 114 yards and zero touchdowns and this interception to Sterling Moore.

However, when Flynn and the Pack came out for the second half, it was a completely different team and following a 60-yard run from Eddie Lacy connected with Jordy Nelson on a 13-yard touchdown to cap a four-play touchdown drive to give the Packers life and the momentum they needed.

Flynn played like the man he is starting in place of, Aaron Rodgers in the final 30 minutes with two touchdowns in the third and two more in the fourth. After missing on the potential game-winning score two plays earlier, Lacy took the handoff from Flynn and lept in to the end zone for the go-ahead score to give the Packers a 37-36 lead to complete the comeback.

“This is going to go down as one of the worst defeats in the history of the Dallas Cowboys,” Fox announcer Joe Buck said after an interception by Tramon Williams with less than two minutes remaining.

The Cowboys led 26-3 at halftime and were outscored 34-10 in the second half as the Packers keep their playoff hopes alive and could be getting Rodgers back next weekend vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers in a rematch of Super Bowl XLV.

Meanwhile, the Cowboys will be losing a lot of sleep over this unfathomable loss as Flynn led touchdown drives on five straight second half possessions to do something Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers haven’t done and that’s win in Dallas.

2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game

The game was played at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas

The [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") played an [American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") game against the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") in Week 15 of the [2013 National Football League (NFL) season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NFL_season "2013 NFL season") on December 15, 2013, at [AT&T Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium "AT&T Stadium") in [Arlington, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_Texas "Arlington, Texas"), United States. Both teams entered Week 15 with middling records, with the Packers sitting at 6–6–1 and the Cowboys at 7–6. The Packers started the season strong, yet a broken collarbone by quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") in Week 8 saw the Packers lose or tie five straight games under three different back-up quarterbacks. Both teams were coming off a loss in Week 14, although each of their playoff hopes were still alive and both still had a chance to win their respective divisions. The Cowboys started the game strong, taking a 26–3 lead going into halftime, with kicker [Dan Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Bailey_/(American_football/) "Dan Bailey (American football)") converting four field goals. [Matt Flynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Flynn_/(American_football/) "Matt Flynn (American football)"), who was playing in place of the injured Rodgers, helped the Packers storm back in the second half. He led the Packers to five touchdown drives, including four touchdown passes. The Packers defense was able to hold the Cowboys to just 10 points in the second half, with [Tramon Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tramon_Williams "Tramon Williams") sealing the victory with an interception of quarterback [Tony Romo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") with less than two minutes left in the game. The victory matched the Packers team record for the largest comeback at 23 points and helped them maintain the possibility of winning the [NFC North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_North "NFC North") and making the playoffs. Both teams entered the final week of the season with a chance to win their division; the Packers won, while the Cowboys lost. The Packers would make the playoffs yet lose in the first round to the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers"). The [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") began the season as the defending [NFC North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_North "NFC North") champions, having won the division the previous two seasons.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-1) They began their season with a record of 5–2, although one of their losses came after surrendering a 16-point second half lead to the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-2013PACK-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-3) Their eighth game of the year was on _[Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday_Night_Football "Monday Night Football")_ against the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"). In the first quarter, [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") was injured, missing the rest of the game with what was later diagnosed as a broken collarbone.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-4) Rodgers would go on to miss the next seven games, with [Seneca Wallace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seneca_Wallace "Seneca Wallace"), [Scott Tolzien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Tolzien "Scott Tolzien"), and [Matt Flynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Flynn_/(American_football/) "Matt Flynn (American football)") all starting games in his place. Wallace was injured in his first game and the Packers signed Flynn, who had played for the Packers previously, midway through the season.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-5) The Packers went 0–4–1 during a five-game stretch which included the Bears game to bring their record to 5–6–1.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-2013PACK-2) The Packers played the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons") in Week 14 and fell behind 21–10 in the first half. However, Flynn led a comeback to beat the Falcons 22–21, evening the Packers record at 6–6–1 and keeping them in the hunt for the NFC North.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-6) The [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") began the 2013 season having gone 8–8 in back-to-back seasons, missing the playoffs both times.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-7) The season was back-and-forth, with the Cowboys never winning more than two games in a row nor losing more than two games in a row. They entered Week 15 with a record of 7–6 after a loss to the Bears in Week 14.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-2013COW-8) The Cowboys were scheduled to host the Packers in Week 15 at [AT&T Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium "AT&T Stadium") on December 15, 2013.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PREVIEW-9) Both teams were mathematically still in the hunt for their respective division titles and needed a victory to improve their chances of making the playoffs.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PREVIEW-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBraun201414-10) The Cowboys were favored by four points.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-11) The Cowboys started the game with possession of the ball. A 27-yard pass from [Tony Romo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") to [Terrance Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrance_Williams "Terrance Williams") got the Cowboys in scoring position, but the Packers got a stop on third down and forced a 47-yard field goal attempt, which [Dan Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Bailey_/(American_football/) "Dan Bailey (American football)") converted. The Packers matched the Cowboys on the next drive, going 41 yards in 6 plays to set-up a 57-yard field goal attempt. Almost all of the yardage on the drive came from a 39-yard pass from [Matt Flynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Flynn_/(American_football/) "Matt Flynn (American football)") to [James Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Jones_/(wide_receiver/) "James Jones (wide receiver)"). [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") converted the field goal, tying the game at 3–3. On the subsequent drive, [DeMarco Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeMarco_Murray "DeMarco Murray") had a 41-yard rush that put the Cowboys in scoring position, but again the Packers stopped the Cowboys on third down, with Bailey converting a 23-yard field goal to give the Cowboys the lead again, 6–3. After the Packers went [three-and-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-and-out "Three-and-out") and punted, the Cowboys quickly drove 65 yards in 4 plays, capped off by a 25-yard touchdown from Romo to [Jason Witten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Witten "Jason Witten"). The Cowboys lead increased to 13–3. On the first play of the next drive, Flynn threw deep to Jones and the Cowboys were called for a 31-yard defensive pass interference penalty. However, after a sack and two incomplete passes, the Packers were forced to punt again. Each team then exchanged punts after short drives. The Cowboys got the ball back and drove 48 yards in 8 plays, but again were stopped and had to attempt a field goal. Bailey converted his third field goal of the half, this time from 43 yards, to increase the Cowboys lead to 16–3. On the next drive, Flynn threw an interception to [Sterling Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling_Moore "Sterling Moore"), who returned it 21 yards. The Packers did not allow the Cowboys to gain any yardage on their drive, but they were already in field goal range. Bailey made his fourth field goal of the half, this time from 50 yards, bringing the score to 19–3. The Packers were again forced to punt on their next drive. Romo completed three passes on the next drive for a combined 70 yards, with Murray scoring a touchdown on a one-yard rush. The Packers attempted to score on the next drive, but they ran out of a time after a 34-yard screen pass from Flynn to [Eddie Lacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Lacy "Eddie Lacy") ended the first half. The Cowboys led 26–3 at halftime.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PLAYBYPLAY-12) The Packers had possession of the ball to begin the second half. On the first play of their drive, Lacy had a 60-yard rush; three plays later Flynn threw a touchdown pass to [Jordy Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordy_Nelson "Jordy Nelson"), cutting the Cowboys lead to 26–10. The Cowboys responded, with Bailey kicking his fifth field goal, from 50 yards, of the game after an 11-play, 48-yard drive. On the ensuing drive, the Packers again travelled the length of the field, going 80 yards in 12 plays, and scoring on a 3-yard touchdown pass from Flynn to [Andrew Quarless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Quarless "Andrew Quarless"). After the Cowboys' field goal and Packers' touchdown, the score was 29–17. The Packers forced a three-and-out on the Cowboys' next drive after sacking Romo on third down. [Micah Hyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micah_Hyde_/(American_football/) "Micah Hyde (American football)") returned the Cowboys' punt from mid-field 26 yards. The Packers scored five plays later on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Flynn to [James Starks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Starks "James Starks"). The Cowboys lead was now only five points, 29–24. On the Cowboys next drive, Romo threw a pass that appeared to be intercepted by [Tramon Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tramon_Williams "Tramon Williams"), however after replay review, the pass was called incomplete. The Cowboys capitalized, going the length of the field to score a touchdown on a short pass from Romo to [Dez Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dez_Bryant "Dez Bryant"). The Packers responded, going 80 yards in 10 plays to score, with Flynn completing a 3-yard pass to Jones for a touchdown. The Cowboys lead was cut back to five points again, with the score at 36–31. The Cowboys converted a third down with 12 yards to go on the next drive, but on the fifth play Romo threw an interception to [Sam Shields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Shields "Sam Shields") at mid-field. The Packers drove to the Cowboys' one-yard line with less than two minutes left in the game. Lacy scored a touchdown on a one-yard rush, with the Packers failing on the two-point conversion. Down for the first time in the game, 37–36, the Cowboys began their next drive with a nine-yard completion from Romo to [Cole Beasley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Beasley "Cole Beasley"). Romo's next pass was ruled incomplete, yet after replay review, the call was changed to an interception by Williams. The Packers ran out the rest of the game clock to secure the comeback victory.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PLAYBYPLAY-12) | Game information | | --- | |

Post-game analysis focused on the Packers’ comeback and the significant differences for each team between the first and second half.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-VANDERMAUSE-16)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FEELING-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-18) The Packers' offense was only able to score three points in the first half, even though the Cowboys came into the game with the worst ranked defense in the NFL.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-THICK1-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-THICK2-20) The Packers' defense was able to stop the Cowboys offense on four drives, forcing field goals instead of touchdowns.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PFRBOX-14) Even so, the Cowboys offense was able to move the ball through the air and on the ground and took a commanding 26–3 lead into halftime.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-THICK1-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-THICK2-20) Coming into the second half, the Packers decided to run the ball, with Lacy breaking free for a 60-yard rush that multiple players noted sparked the Packers’ offense.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-RUSHING-21) The Packers scored their first touchdown three plays later, starting a streak of five straight touchdown drives.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FEELING-17) Other key plays were highlighted, including interceptions in the fourth quarter by Shields and Williams that helped the Packers gain the lead for the first time and seal their victory.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FEELING-17)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-VANDERMAUSE-16) Individual performances were highlighted, especially on offense. Romo threw for 358 yards and two touchdowns, while Flynn had 299 passing yards and four touchdowns. Each team had a rusher eclipse 100 yards, with Lacy gaining 141 yards and Murray having 134 yards; each scored a touchdown.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NUMBERS-22) Boykin and Quarless led the Packers in receptions and yards, although Nelson’s performance on third down was specifically noted.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NUMBERS-22)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NELSON-23) On the Cowboys’ side, Bryant had a successful performance, catching 11 passes for 153 yards and a touchdown.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NUMBERS-22) His touchdown catch was praised for its level of difficulty.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NFL-24) After the game, decisions by the Cowboys coaching staff and Romo were questioned.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NFL-24) The Cowboys were very successful rushing the ball in the first half, with Murray going for 93 yards. However, in the second half, even with a large lead, the Cowboys only gave the ball to Murray seven times. Ironically, it was the Packers who saw a lot of success in the second half rushing the ball.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-RUSHING-21) This was very apparent on each Cowboys’ drive that ended in an interception, with post-game commentators questioning why the Cowboys were not trying to run out the clock and instead were throwing the ball downfield.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NFL-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-25) Cowboys head coach [Jason Garrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Garrett "Jason Garrett") noted after the game that in hindsight the team should have called more running plays.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-RUSHING-21) After their victory, the Packers record was 7–6–1 and they were still in the hunt for the NFC North title. With Rodgers close to returning, the Packers hosted the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") at [Lambeau Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field") in Week 16. In that game the Packers gave up a late score after a fumble by Flynn, but then had a long kickoff return by Micah Hyde. After a couple plays, the Packers got to the one-yard line, but a penalty pushed them back five yards and gave them just enough time to run a play to try to score. Flynn threw incomplete and the Packers lost, leaving them with 7–7–1 record. The Bears lost in Week 16 as well, setting up a match-up in Week 17 for the NFC North title between the Packers and Bears, who were hosting. Rodgers returned from his injury for the Bears game and threw a late touchdown pass on fourth down to seal the victory and the NFC North title for the Packers.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-BEARS-26) The game against the Bears was named one of the 50 greatest sports moments in Wisconsin history in 2020 by the _[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Journal_Sentinel "Milwaukee Journal Sentinel")_.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-27) The Packers hosted the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers") in the first round of the playoffs, [losing 23–20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_NFL_playoffs#NFC:_San_Francisco_49ers_23,_Green_Bay_Packers_20 "2013–14 NFL playoffs") and ending their season.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-28) The Cowboys recovered the next week, beating the [Washington Redskins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Redskins "Washington Redskins") and setting up another winner-take-all game for the [NFC East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_East "NFC East") division title against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles") in Week 17.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-29) The Cowboys lost 24–22, with a late interception keeping them from getting into field goal range near the end of the game.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-MISS-30) The loss gave the Eagles the division title and caused the Cowboys to miss the playoffs for the fourth straight season.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-MISS-30)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-31) The 23-point comeback victory tied the Packers' record for the largest comeback in franchise history.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-32)[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-33) The previous 23-point comeback came during [a 1982 regular season game against the Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Los_Angeles_Rams%E2%80%93Green_Bay_Packers_game "1982 Los Angeles Rams–Green Bay Packers game"). The _[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Journal_Sentinel "Milwaukee Journal Sentinel")_ highlighted the game as one of the Packers' biggest fourth quarter comebacks, with the team down 12 points heading into the last quarter.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-34) It was also the second notable game where Flynn had a big outing as a back-up to Rodgers, after the [final game of the 2011 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Flynn_Game "Matt Flynn Game").[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-BEARS-26) In a 2024 article comparing the similarities between the 2013 and 2024 Packers seasons, the _[Wisconsin State Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_State_Journal "Wisconsin State Journal")_ noted that Flynn helped engineer "a miraculous come-from-behind win" while providing enough contributions "to keep the Packers alive for a playoff berth".[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-35) In his book game.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristl2021867-36) The victory helped the Packers keep their playoffs hopes alive, ultimately becoming necessary for them to win the NFC North.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-37)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-BEARS-26)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-38) rivalry");[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-39)[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-40) Cowboy Dez Bryant says he left game early so no one would see him cry
=====================================================================

By Sam Farmer

Dec. 16, 2013 12 AM PT

Dallas Cowboys receiver Dez Bryant explained Monday that he ran to the locker room before the end of the loss to Green Bay because he didn’t want to be seen crying on the sideline.

“I was wrong,” Bryant told reporters during a visit to Cook Children’s Medical Center in Fort Worth, Texas, according to ESPN.com. “It didn’t have anything to do with my teammates. I just ... I couldn’t watch Green Bay kneel the ball down on the field after a tough loss like that.

“I was very emotional. I cried when I got to the locker room. I didn’t want to show that stuff on the sideline.”

Advertisement

Bryant had 11 catches for 153 yards and a touchdown in the 37-36 loss at home, a game in which the Cowboys had been favored by a touchdown.

On his weekly radio show, Cowboys Coach Jason Garrett said he planned to address the early departure with Bryant later Monday.

“I understand why to a certain extent,” Garrett said on 105.3 The Fan. “They’re kneeling the ball, the game essentially is over. He’s an emotional guy. We’re all very emotional about what we do.

Advertisement

“But he needs to stay out on the field and I’ll address that with him today. And just explain why it’s important to do that, and he’ll understand.”

The larger lesson? Mommas don’t let your Cowboys grow up to be babies.

December 16, 2013 - Aaron Wilson

Dez Bryant leaves field early, says he was 'emotional'
------------------------------------------------------

Why did Dallas Cowboys star wide receiver Dez Bryant head into the locker room with time remaining in a loss to the Green Bay Packers?

He told reporters he was too upset.

Bryant went inside following quarterback Tony Romo's second interception in the fourth quarter. Bryant finished the game with 11 receptions for 153 yards and one touchdown.

"I walked back to the locker room because I was emotional," Bryant wrote on Twitter. "It had nothing to do with my teammates we had it... We fought and didn't finish."

Today, Bryant apologized for leaving early.

“I was wrong,” Bryant said, per ESPN Dallas. “It didn’t have anything to do with my teammates. I couldn’t watch Green Bay kneel the ball down on the field after a tough loss like that. I was very emotional. I cried when I got into the locker room. I didn’t want to show that stuff on the sideline. ..

“Whenever I’m out on the football field, it’s all about the team. “I’m a team guy and that’s what I think about and that’s what I focus on. I extremely, extremely apologize for leaving, but my teammates and coaches understand. I am a very emotional player and we didn’t finish. It had nothing to do with my teammates."

Greenbay Packers beat Cowboys
=============================

by [![Image 3](https://www.gravatar.com/avatar/2c49db255ede7cd47bec52f8c8553660?s=40&r=g&d=mm) **ufl**](https://ufl-football.com/members/ufl/ "Posts by ufl") December 16, 2013, 2:01 pm **387** Views

[Share](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fufl-football.com%2F2013%2F12%2F16%2Fgreenbay-packers-beat-cowboys%2F)[Tweet](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Greenbay%20Packers%20beat%20Cowboys&url=https://ufl-football.com/2013/12/16/greenbay-packers-beat-cowboys/)

In the first half of the match the Greenbay Packers were down and looked as though they were out but no in the second half the packers managed to win by 37-36 in a amazing game of football which you dont see often.

The packers managed to do the unimaginable by scoring touchdowns in all five of their second half possessions thanks largely due to there quarterback Matt flynn.

In this game it wasnt as though the cowboys were playing badly as they managed to break records in the first half with 332 in the first half putting them in the lead by 23 points. At half time the Cowboys were winning by 26-3 and it looked as though the packers were going to be humiliated in the next half.

It was a really tight game, even in the last eight minutes fans didn’t know who was going to win as the Cowboys managed to grab a 12 point lead after a super touchdown from Dez Bryant.

But it was a few mistakes near the end of the match by the cowboys that meant it was the packers who won and not them. Tony Romo with a really bad pass to Miles Austin meant that in the final minutes of the games Sam shields was able to then make sure that the Packers get the win.

There was a last chance for the cowboys to snatch it back at the very end but Romo also mucked up again with his next interception he could not deliver the ball over to Cole Beasley which put the last nail in the coffin for the Cowboys.

Romo may have lost it for the Cowboys… Romo with the first interception could have played the ball to Miles Austin however the packers put pressure on Romo, which made him crumble and produce such a poor throw. He didn’t have to pass to Miles Austin when he did he could still have did a run-pass trow instead but maybe the pressure mucked up his decision making process.

Despite the fight the Cowboys put up in this football game it wasn’t enough. The cowboys are on the brink of early elimination.

The Packers however are as strong as ever thanks to Flynn delivering as expected. The great quarterback really did show off his talent in this game after five very impressive touchdown one after another.

\-2 players in the game were injured which were Justin Durant from the Cowboy team and Johnny Jolly from the Packers.

![Image 2](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_fill,w_720,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/shape/cover/sport/28f441a5fdde159ea9ff929fea6a030bc47bc2820da824188e23e2c22d741134.jpg)

![Image 3: Dec 15, 2013; Arlington, TX, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Matt Flynn (10) reacts to a touchdown with tight end Andrew Quarless (81) in the fourth quarter at AT](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_fill,w_16,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/shape/cover/sport/d093b6ebc926da1c79d2d65eb9e388c652f7d94af097750e5a210202f084087b.jpg)

Dec 15, 2013; Arlington, TX, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Matt Flynn (10) reacts to a touchdown with tight end Andrew Quarless (81) in the fourth quarter at AT

The Green Bay Packers were trailing the Dallas Cowboys 26-3 at the half, and even they thought they were done. Packers quarterback Matt Flynn said even they though the game was over.

“When we were in the locker room at halftime, did we really think there was a chance, the way we played, that we could come back and win the game? Not really,” Flynn told [TheMMQB.com’s Peter King](http://mmqb.si.com/2013/12/16/nfl-week-15-monday-morning-quarterback/6/) after the game.

It was a big win for a man who has had a rough season. Flynn had been cut twice in 2013 since being released by the Seattle Seahawks. At home with the Packers, where he was successful before going to Seattle, Flynn brought back some of that magic.

“It’s all worth it now,” Flynn said. “This is the best day I’ve had in the NFL. You work for a long time to have the kind of fun we had today, and if you have to go through some tough times to get there, well, thatâ€™s the way it goes.”

8.title: RGV6IEJyeWFudCBlbW90aW9uYWwsIGV4aXRzIERhbGxhcyBDb3dib3lzJyBsb3NzIGVhcmx5
8.content:
Published: Dec 16, 2013 at 12:38 AM

"[Dez Bryant](https://www.nfl.com/player/dezbryant/497278/profile) leaving the field was absolutely, 100 percent, positively wrong. Can't do it under any circumstances," said Deion Sanders, an NFL Media analyst and [Hall of Fame](http://www.profootballhof.com/) cornerback who played for the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL).

The word "emotional" was the rationale used by Bryant and his teammates for the wide receiver's early exit.

> I walked back to the locker room because I was emotional...it had nothing to do with my teammates we had it... We fought and didn't finish
> 
> — Dez Bryant (@DezBryant) [December 16, 2013](https://twitter.com/DezBryant/status/412397676924108801?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

On his weekly radio show with KRLD-FM in Dallas, [Jason Garrett](https://www.nfl.com/player/jasongarrett/2514652/profile) defended Bryant on Monday by saying, "Dez is one of the [great team guys](https://twitter.com/DesmondPurnell/status/412580022352760832) I've ever been around ... He loves his teammates, but you [have to understand](https://twitter.com/DesmondPurnell/status/412580378725974016) how to handle yourself ... he'll learn from this situation."

Bryant took some time Monday, during a visit to the Cook Children's Medical Center in Fort Worth, to address his decision to walk off the field.

"I was wrong," Bryant said, [via the Fort Worth Star-Telegram](http://sportsblogs.star-telegram.com/cowboys/2013/12/dez-bryant-regrets-early-exit.html). "It didn't have anything to do with my teammates. I just ... I couldn't watch Green Bay kneel the ball down on the field after a tough loss like that.

"I was very emotional. I cried when I got into the locker room. I didn't want to show that stuff on the sideline."

This will be a storyline that takes the focus off the second-half debacle the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) delivered Sunday.

17.title: Q293Ym95cyBGYW5zOiBTYXkgR29vZGJ5ZSBUbyBKYXNvbiBHYXJyZXR0
17.content:
Dec 15, 2013; Arlington, TX, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo (9) reacts after getting sacked in the fourth quarter against the Green Bay Packers at AT

Forget the 2013 season.  It’s over.  Yeah, yeah I know the Cowboys are not mathematically eliminated and if Philadelphia lost to Minnesota than it is completely rational to think they will also do so to the Bears and even Dallas but forget it.  It won’t matter.  Why?

Because the Dallas Cowboys will not win another game this season.

Blame it on the quarterback who can’t shake the rep of a choker, mainly because he continues to feed it at the most inopportune times.

Blame it on the defense who can’t stop a first string or second string or third string quarterback from leading his team up and down the field at will.

Blame it on the injuries… like other teams don’t have those too.

Blame it on the egotistical, delusional owner who thinks he has a team so close to a championship.

Blame whoever and whatever, it doesn’t matter.  This team accomplished its goal.  The Dallas Cowboys will not finish 8-8 this season…

They’ll finish 7-9.

In the latest mind-blowing, gut-wrenching, train wreck of a game, Dallas once again found a way to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory.  Up 26-3 (you know, much like the Lions game from 2011 which you can relive here if yesterday was not already enough pain – [http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110020dal.htm](http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110020dal.htm)…) DeMarco Murray was only given the ball seven times even though…

A. He had 93 yards and a touchdown prior to that point.  
B. He was averaging 5.85 yards per carry on those final seven runs.  
C. Dallas had a lead almost the entire time.  
D. Running the ball keeps the clock going and when coupled with an almost six yard average likely means you will gain multiple first downs.

The excruciating thing is that I have mentioned twice in the last couple of weeks that the Cowboys are undefeated when Murray gets twenty carries.  This game, he got eighteen.  Two more would have likely ended the game in a much different manner.  With 2:58 left on the clock, Green Bay had just used their second time out to stop the clock after Murray got four yards on first down.  Instead of running the ball once more to exhaust the Packers’ final time out and likely gain more yards, a play-action pass was called.  Green Bay sent a run blitz because, you know, the Cowboys SHOULD BE RUNNING THE BALL HERE and was able to force a bad throw from Romo who was moving away from his body.  Interception.  Running the ball twice would have definitely eliminated the Packers from stopping the clock.  It’s also fair to assume, that even factoring Murray getting half his average per carry, Dallas would have picked up the last first down needed to win.

I am aware that it was Romo’s decision to change the play to a pass.  Assuming that is true, he should no longer be given to deviate from the play call.  Yet and still, Garrett is supposed to be the HEAD COACH.  He took ownership of the play call process (their favorite word).  He has a voice and it should be the loudest.  For Garrett to not impose his voice and demand sticking to the original call to run it shows a weakness that cannot be tolerated from someone in a position of authority.  That one play does not answer why there were not other attempts with a bigger margin for error to continue to attack on the ground.

So now, with yet another lost season coming to an end, one has to wonder if the defensive coordinator will not be the only change that is made this offseason.  If Jerry is ever serious about winning, it is clear that it cannot be done with the current regime.  Three years and a few other games of nearly pristine mediocrity was enough to make a change.  The robotic coach speak and constant refrain of “process” and “all three phrases” rhetoric falls on deaf ears when there is no improvement to behold.  The countdown to Garrett’s firing began when the clock read 0:00 Sunday night.

TOO PAINFUL TO WATCH: Dez Bryant explains why he walked off the field
=====================================================================

By [robertdknight](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/author/robertdknight/) on 12/16/2013

[![Image 1: TOO PAINFUL TO WATCH - Dez Bryant explains why he walked off the field - Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers - Dez Bryant crying cry cries](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/too-painful-to-watch-dez-bryant-explains-why-he-walked-off-the-field-dallas-cowboys-vs-gree1.png?w=640&h=331)](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/too-painful-to-watch-dez-bryant-explains-why-he-walked-off-the-field-dallas-cowboys-vs-gree.png)

Dallas Cowboys receiver Dez Bryant took to Twitter last night to explain why he walked to the locker room with 1:21 left in the 37-36 loss to the Packers.

It came after the game-sealing interception from quarterback Tony Romo. Bryant walked off **after** the replay officials reversed the call on the field that the pass was incomplete, giving the interception to cornerback Tramon Williams.

Bryant, after declining to speak with reporters after the game, later explained his actions in a tweet on @dezbryant:

> “I walked back to the locker room because I was emotional…it had nothing to do with my teammates we had it… We fought and didn’t finish.”

Bryant was the only Cowboys player to leave the field early, but quarterback Tony Romo refused to criticize him for his actions.

> “It’s an emotional game,” Romo said. “You get to the end there, obviously, it’s not fun for any of us to lose a football game. It’s not an enjoyable process the way it ends, no matter how it ends. It’s always tough emotionally so it is what it is.”

Bryant had a solid game, finishing with 11 catches for 153 yards and a touchdowns. However, he could have had better numbers as Romo underthrew him on two deep balls and overthrew him on another in the end zone.

> “I think the worst thing you can do sometimes with Dez is overthrow him,” Romo said. “Obviously, you’d like to hit him perfectly in stride. He’s such a great athlete, he comes down with most of them. I look back and I wish I had one or two where I gave it a little bit more. But usually, I make sure if I err ever it’s slightly less because he always goes up and gets it. Obviously, I look back, I’ll push those down the field if I have that opportunity.”

**RELATED: Dez Bryant couldn’t stand to watch Green Bay kneel the ball down**

[![Image 2: TOO PAINFUL TO WATCH - Dez Bryant explains why he walked off the field - Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers - Dez Bryant remarkable TD touchdown 2](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/too-painful-to-watch-dez-bryant-explains-why-he-walked-off-the-field-dallas-cowboys-vs-gree1.jpg?w=640&h=427)](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/too-painful-to-watch-dez-bryant-explains-why-he-walked-off-the-field-dallas-cowboys-vs-gree.jpg)

Dez Bryant regrets it. He wishes he wouldn’t have walked off the field with 1:21 left and the Green Bay Packers a couple kneels away from a 37-36 victory over the Dallas Cowboys.

Bryant spoke about the incident Monday morning as the Cowboys were on their annual visits to area children’s hospitals, which included Bryant visiting Cook Children’s Medical Center in Fort Worth.

> “I was wrong,” Bryant said. “It didn’t have anything to do with my teammates. I just … I couldn’t watch Green Bay kneel the ball down on the field after a tough loss like that.
> 
> “I was very emotional. I cried when I got into the locker room. I didn’t want to show that stuff on the sideline.”

The Cowboys blew a 23-point halftime lead and wasted an impressive performance by Bryant. He had 11 catches for 153 yards and a touchdown. The TD catch might have been the most remarkable of all, as he grabbed the ball away from several Green Bay defenders and kept his feet inbounds near the back of the end zone.

[![Image 3: TOO PAINFUL TO WATCH - Dez Bryant explains why he walked off the field - Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers - Dez Bryant remarkable TD touchdown](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/too-painful-to-watch-dez-bryant-explains-why-he-walked-off-the-field-dallas-cowboys-vs-gree3.jpg?w=640&h=360)](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/too-painful-to-watch-dez-bryant-explains-why-he-walked-off-the-field-dallas-cowboys-vs-gree2.jpg)

But that catch was overshadowed by Bryant’s early exit.

> “Whenever I’m out on the football field, it’s all about the team,” Bryant said. “I’m a team guy and that’s what I think about and that’s what I focus on. I extremely, extremely apologize for leaving, but my teammates and coaches understand. I am a very emotional player and we didn’t finish.”

The hospital visit, though, did provide some comfort for Bryant and the other players to get away from the tough loss by bringing smiles to children’s faces.

> “This is something I really enjoy doing,” Bryant said. “Whenever you’re able to make someone’s day, you should feel good about it.”

_**[![Image 4: TOO PAINFUL TO WATCH - Dez Bryant explains why he walked off the field - Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers - Dez Bryant charity](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/too-painful-to-watch-dez-bryant-explains-why-he-walked-off-the-field-dallas-cowboys-vs-gree5.jpg?w=360&h=480)](https://theboysareback.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/too-painful-to-watch-dez-bryant-explains-why-he-walked-off-the-field-dallas-cowboys-vs-gree4.jpg)**_

_**Editor’s Comment:** I’m going to share my own opinion of this situation. If you have one, I encourage you to express it in the comment section below. The media at large is making light of Dez Bryant’s emotional and tearful reaction to this loss. No, he shouldn’t have left. No, he will not do it again._

_If you follow the Dallas Cowboys closely (like most regular visitors on this site), you already know how emotional Dez Bryant is. That’s a big part of his personality. HE’S DETERMINED TO WIN! The coaches and players are quick to point out that his emotions are one of the key elements that make his such a valuable member of the team. Most of the players that Jason Garrett has kept with his team, or brought in, have the same type of workmanlike traits. The thing with Dez is that he wears his emotions on his sleeve. He’s outwardly expressive. I think that’s a good thing and also believe it’s something that this locker room needs. A player that HATES losing that bad needs to be heard. With only two games remaining, this could be something that ignites or unites this team. They sure need it. The players on this roster want to win for Jason Garrett, the coaches … and veterans Tony Romo, Jason Witten, and DeMarcus Ware. You can add Dez Bryant to that list._

Photo above: Dallas Cowboys on their annual visits to area children’s hospitals, which included Bryant visiting Cook Children’s Medical Center in Fort Worth.

Published: Dec 15, 2013 at 01:58 PM

Flynn threw four touchdown passes in the second half, [Eddie Lacy](https://www.nfl.com/player/eddielacy/2540168/profile) had the winning score on a 1-yard plunge after an interception by [Tony Romo](https://www.nfl.com/player/tonyromo/2505354/profile) gave them one more chance, and the [Green Bay Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) matched the biggest comeback in franchise history in a 37-36 win over the [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) on Sunday.

Romo tossed two interceptions in the final 3 minutes, the first one giving Green Bay a chance for the go-ahead score with the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) in position to run out the clock with a 36-31 lead.

Lacy scored with 1:31 to go for Green Bay's first lead since the first quarter and after the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) trailed 26-3 at halftime.

"It took me everything not to cry," said [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) coach [Mike McCarthy](https://www.nfl.com/player/mikemccarthy/2520528/profile), whose team won its second straight without Rodgers after going winless in the first five, including the Chicago game when the star QB got hurt. "I'm just drained. Just the sheer emotion. It was incredible."

Playing on the same field where Rodgers was the MVP when they won the 2011 [Super Bowl](http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/47), the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) matched the 1982 team in a September game against the Los Angeles [Rams](https://www.nfl.com/teams/st.louisrams/profile?team=STL) for the largest rally.

The [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) (7-6-1) kept their playoff hopes alive with Rodgers possibly returning next week. He was close to medical clearance, but missed his sixth straight game with a broken collarbone. He was wearing on a headset on Green Bay's sideline.

"Most guys would pack it in - 'Guys, it's not our season. Let's go home and get ready for next year,'" said Green Bay cornerback [Tramon Williams](https://www.nfl.com/player/tramonwilliams/2506789/profile), who had an interception overturned on review before a game-clinching pick that was ruled incomplete and reversed on replay. "It's not that vibe here."

The vibe in Dallas could negative for a while, with [Dez Bryant](https://www.nfl.com/player/dezbryant/497278/profile) walking off the field before the game ended and refusing to talk to reporters in the locker room, simply shaking his head at them after finishing with 153 yards and a touchdown.

"This is one of the hardest losses that I've experienced," [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) owner Jerry Jones said. "That's a shame that we've lost that ballgame."

The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) (7-7) blew a great chance to pull even with Philadelphia in the NFC East but still control their playoff fate. They finish with Washington and the [Eagles](https://www.nfl.com/teams/philadelphiaeagles/profile?team=PHI).

"We still control what we feel like we can get done," Romo said. "It just doesn't feel like it right now because we let it slip away."

With Dallas leading 36-31, Bryant made a lunging first down after a catch just before the 2-minute warning that looked as if it would Dallas help hold off a huge Green Bay rally. But Romo threw behind [Miles Austin](https://www.nfl.com/player/milesaustin/2495801/profile) after escaping a sack and [Sam Shields](https://www.nfl.com/player/samshields/1037374/profile) intercepted at midfield.

The [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) steadily moved downfield before the plunge by Lacy, who had 141 yards rushing.

Behind for the first time since the first quarter, Romo threw a ball too far in front of [Cole Beasley](https://www.nfl.com/player/colebeasley/2535698/profile), and Williams made a diving grab that was initially called incomplete. When the video review overturned the call, Flynn ended the game with kneel-downs.

"Right now, words really have no effect," Dallas cornerback [Brandon Carr](https://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/profile) said. "Complete debacle the second half. We've just got to get better, man."

Williams had an earlier interception overturned on review with Dallas clinging to a 29-24 lead. He cradled a deflected pass in his arms and had a weaving return to inside the Dallas 10, but replayed showed the nose of ball hitting the turf.

The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) went on to score when Bryant made a leaping grab over [M.D. Jennings](https://www.nfl.com/player/m.d.jennings/2530703/profile) and got two feet down in the back of the end zone for a 36-24 lead.

Flynn answered with his fourth straight scoring drive to get the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) back within five. A Dallas defense that gave up eight straight scoring drives to Chicago in a loss last week let the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) get touchdowns on five straight drives after halftime.

"What a feelin'!'" said Flynn, who threw for 299 yards with one interception. "As we were taking a knee, we were thinking 'Is this real? Is this happening?'"

Romo threw for 358 yards and two touchdowns, but couldn't avoid two more critical mistakes in a career at least partially defined by them.

Packers happy Cowboys abandoned running game
============================================

Published: Dec 16, 2013 at 09:18 AM

![Image 1: Author Image](https://static.www.nfl.com/image/private/t_thumb_squared/t_lazy/f_png/league/wvxg3nqhx25n0kr1npmz.png)

[Chris Wesseling](https://www.nfl.com/author/chris-wesseling-0ap1000000132626)

Around The NFL Podcast Co-Host

*   
*   
*   
*   Copied!

When the [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) lost a [17-16 squeaker](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013091507/2013/REG2/cowboys@chiefs) at Kansas City in September, coach [Jason Garrett](https://www.nfl.com/player/jasongarrett/2514652/profile) conceded that his team simply has to "[run the ball more](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000246155/article/jason-garrett-dallas-cowboys-need-to-run-ball-more)." When [DeMarco Murray](https://www.nfl.com/player/demarcomurray/2495207/profile) averaged 7.75 yards on just four carries in a narrow [27-23 win](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013110302/2013/REG9/vikings@cowboys) over the [Vikings](https://www.nfl.com/teams/minnesotavikings/profile?team=MIN) in early November, Garrett stated a renewed commitment to [a more balanced offense](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000276479/article/dallas-cowboys-lack-balance-without-rushing-attack).

All of those pledges to institute a consistent ground attack went out the window Sunday. [Tony Romo](https://www.nfl.com/player/tonyromo/2505354/profile) attempted 48 passes in a game he led 26-3, 29-10 and 36-24 at various points in the second half.

**On NFL Network**  
_NFL Replay_  
will re-air the [Green Bay Packers' 37-36 win](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013121512/2013/REG15/packers@cowboys?icampaign=ATL_newsdriver) over the [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) from Week 15 on Wednesday, Dec. 18 at 9 p.m. ET.

» **[NFL Network schedule](http://www.nfl.com/nflnetwork/networkschedule)**

The victorious [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) were perplexed yet grateful for the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL)' much-derided, [soap operatic play-calling](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000288747/article/jerry-jones-wilsons-move-key-to-cowboys-play-calls).

"We watched (Murray) last week with the coaches and we said, 'This guy is the real deal,'" [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) defensive tackle [Ryan Pickett](https://www.nfl.com/player/ryanpickett/2504763/profile) said, via the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel's Bob McGinn. "He's tough, fast and so deceptively strong. He's one of the most underrated backs.

"Oh, my God. It's the best zone scheme in the league," Pickett continued. "The last four weeks, nobody could stop it -- their zone scheme. [And they gave up on it](http://www.jsonline.com/sports/packers/bizarre-cowboys-play-calling-spurs-historic-packers-comeback-b99164140z1-235969701.html?ipad=y). We're just happy they did. We were, like, 'OK, we'll take it.'"

Pickett wasn't the only Green Bay player to express astonishment at Dallas' refusal to lean on Murray with a commanding lead.

[Matt Flynn](http://www.nfl.com/voting/never-say-never/2013/REG/15#playerid:0ap2000000298789)

[](http://www.nfl.com/voting/never-say-never/2013/REG/15#playerid:0ap2000000298789)

"That's just who they are," cornerback [Tramon Williams](https://www.nfl.com/player/tramonwilliams/2506789/profile) said. "They run the ball really well against everybody they play, but they just never stick with it."

The highlight of McGinn's masterpiece of a game recap was Pickett's acknowledgment that his teammates knew they could recover from Dallas' first-half roundhouses to pull off a historic comeback "even with [Matt Flynn](https://www.nfl.com/player/mattflynn/367/profile)" as the quarterback.

After pointing out Romo's [game-changing error](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000298872/article/jason-garrett-tony-romo-shouldve-handed-off-on-int) in the heartbreaking loss, an incessantly passive Garrett offered another empty promise Monday to [run the ball and maintain balance](http://espn.go.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/107452/garrett-we-should-have-run-the-ball-more).

Garrett's penchant for abandoning the run while finding [creative ways to lose tight games](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299491/article/tony-romos-10-most-heartbreaking-losses) raises two questions:

[Eddie Lacy](http://www.nfl.com/voting/players-air-and-ground/2013/REG/15#playerid:0ap2000000299425)

[](http://www.nfl.com/voting/players-air-and-ground/2013/REG/15#playerid:0ap2000000299425)

Does the coaching staff have [any semblance of faith](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000265765/article/demarco-murray-not-dallas-cowboys-franchise-back) in Murray's ability to stay healthy [under a heavy workload](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000292447/article/cowboys-still-looking-for-demarco-murray-complement)?

Is owner Jerry Jones going to [continue to deflect](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299431/article/jerry-jones-no-need-for-weekly-jason-garrett-pledge) all queries into [Garrett's job security](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000285458/article/jason-garrett-will-coach-dallas-cowboys-next-season) as his team lags behind in game-planning, play-calling and time management?

\*The latest "[Around The League Podcast](http://www.nfl.com/podcast/aroundtheleague-podcast/1387170744000/detail)" broke down the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) loss and [every other Week 15 game](http://www.nfl.com/podcast/aroundtheleague-podcast/1387170744000/detail). \*

Tramon Williams' game-saver sets off wild celebration
=====================================================

Second try with replay seals Packers’ historic comeback
-------------------------------------------------------

Dec 15, 2013 at 12:51 PM

![Image 3: Author Image](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_thumb_squared/t_lazy/f_auto/packers/na5aagldsavrxnrbygad.jpg)

[Mike Spofford](https://www.packers.com/author/mike-spofford)

packers.com editor

[](https://twitter.com/mikespofford)

*   
*   
*   
*   Copied!

![Image 4: 131215-lockerroom-300.jpg](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/t_lazy/f_auto/packers/wmljeyvekpsi1bysbldw.jpg)

DALLAS—When the replay review with less than 90 seconds left on Sunday reversed the call of incomplete pass and gave Tramon Williams the game-saving interception, the Packers sideline was up for grabs.

"I haven't felt this way in a long time – I feel like we won a Super Bowl," said linebacker Clay Matthews, echoing the comments of several of his teammates who compared the jubilation of Sunday's wild comeback for a 37-36 victory over the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium to the Packers' only previous visit here, three seasons ago for Super Bowl XLV.

"Our sideline was jumping," receiver James Jones said, "like we did win the Super Bowl."

It was a comeback for the ages as the Packers rallied from a 23-point hole, tying the largest deficit overcome in team history 31 years ago.

Strangely enough, the replay booth not long before appeared to quash the Packers' hopes, when Williams' diving interception early in the fourth quarter was overturned. Referee Walt Coleman said the ball hit the ground between Williams' arms, nullifying the turnover and Williams' weaving return to the Dallas 7-yard line with the Packers trailing 29-24.

Dallas went on to score a touchdown on that drive, but the Packers still managed to score twice more and regain the lead by one point, needing one more stop on defense.

Cowboys QB Tony Romo, who had been intercepted by Sam Shields on the previous drive to set up the Packers' go-ahead TD, threw wide of receiver Cole Beasley, and Williams snared the ball as he dove and spun onto his back, preventing the ball from ever touching the ground. Two series, two picks for the defense, and almost 3-for-3 on the earlier close call.

"The one that I didn't get credited with, I thought I caught it," Williams said. "But the one I did get credit with, I've never felt more sure about a catch in my life."

As a result, Williams gestured manically for replay to take a look at it, and he wouldn't give the ball back to the side judge who ruled the pass incomplete. As Dallas hustled to try to run another play, the Packers called timeout just as the replay official buzzed Coleman.

"The referee was calling for the ball, and I refused to give it to him," Williams said. "He might have asked me about four or five times, and I didn't give him the ball. I saw Mike (McCarthy) running up the sideline and I knew we were going to try to do something."

The Packers did something all right, turning around an abysmal first half that saw them trailing 26-3 with their season on the brink.

The offense came to life, scoring five touchdowns in five second-half possessions, jump-started by Eddie Lacy's 60-yard run on the first snap of the third quarter. From then on, there was seemingly no stopping backup QB Matt Flynn and the offense, as it put together consecutive scoring drives of 80, 80, 22, 80 and 50 yards.

"More or less, we were just saying one play at a time," center Evan Dietrich-Smith said. "We weren't really looking for one guy to make a play, we were just making sure we were making the play on that one play. That just led one thing to another, and we started making a lot of big plays, and the next thing you know we take the lead at the end of the game."

That lead was set up by Shields' interception, which came against a crossing route by receiver Miles Austin. Matthews, whose sack inside the 5-yard line earlier in the fourth quarter set up Micah Hyde's strong punt return for a short field, barely missed sacking Romo a second time.

Shields recovered after getting beat off the line of scrimmage to snare the pass at midfield, giving the Packers a chance, down 36-31 with 2:46 left.

"I tell you what, I was pretty upset within that .5 second of missing the sack and Sam's interception," Matthews said. "But yeah, it was a huge play I think to get him off the spot, get him uncomfortable, let him know someone was coming after him, and then Sam made a heck of a play. Ultimately, that was the difference in the ballgame right there.

"I'm happy we won the game. I'm upset I missed that sack, but who knows, it might have turned out different had I got it."

The Packers will take a nod from the football gods after all they've been through the last two months, and especially the last two weeks.

Down by 11 at halftime to Atlanta a week ago, the Packers rallied. Facing a deficit more than twice as large on Sunday, nobody quit.

"We came into halftime, 26-3, most guys would have packed it in, 'OK guys, it's not our season, let's just go home and get ready for next year,'" Williams said. "Not that vibe here."

Instead there's now a sincere vibe of belief that the season holds promise. Whether or not QB Aaron Rodgers comes back next week, the Packers will be in control of their own postseason destiny if the Lions lose on Monday night to the Ravens. If the Lions win, the Packers still can win the division with two more wins and one more Detroit defeat.

"When you give a team confidence, especially with the team we have and all the players we have and the ability we have, when we believe we can win down by that many points, in any game, we never think we're out?" Jones said. "Look out."

Unsaid by Jones is how far the Packers have come in 2013. A team that couldn't finish strong in the fourth quarter for the first half of the season, even with its starting quarterback, suddenly has come through big-time late in back-to-back games with everything at stake to keep breathing in the NFC playoff chase.

"The adversity we went through, last week, this week, guys continue to fight, continue to fight, continue to fight," Williams said. "You have to feel it's never over for us, truthfully."
